newsitem.title: FRANCE: Radiation at French nuke site abnormal - Greenpeace.
newsitem.headline: Radiation at French nuke site abnormal - Greenpeace.

text.p: Environmental pressure group Greenpeace said on Wednesday that radioactivity measured on a beach near France's nuclear reprocessing plant was up to 3,000 times the normal level.
But the state-owned company Cogema, which operates the plant at La Hague, near Cherbourg in western France, said the radiation level was well below legal norms and no threat to public health.

Greenpeace said measurements taken on Tuesday by experts from the independent Crii-Rad agency on a pipe which carries waste water from the plant to the sea "revealed figures 3,000 times higher than the general level in the atmosphere".
The pipe is usually submerged but was exposed by the unusually big spring tide.

Cogema said in a statement that "only a few metres (yards) of the pipe emerge from the water for a few hours roughly every 10 years, about 100 metres (yards) from the coast and very far from the mouth of the pipe, which is five km (three miles) further".
While insisting that the radiation measured at the site was insignificant, the company said it would nevertheless signpost the site "for these exceptional cases".
